section_summary.extract_value: This section investigates the conditional indirect effects of daily loneliness on gratitude-health associations, proposing loneliness as a psychosocial mechanism. It reports that daily loneliness significantly predicted subjective well-being and self-reported health within a 20-day study. Results from conditional, multilevel indirect effect models revealed that loneliness mediated associations between gratitude and subjective well-being, and gratitude and health symptoms, at the between-person level. These indirect effects were significant for the treatment group but not the control group, supporting moderated mediation, and a strong negative association between gratitude and loneliness was found for the treatment group (N=38) but not the control group.
